event.juno_heart2.1.text: See that color? It should be cherry. It keeps going gray at the edges. ...Okay. We wait for it. Hold steady. Both hands.
event.juno_heart2.1.why: frightened: the forge itself misbehaves; Juno stays practical and keeps the player's hands busy

event.juno_heart2.1.text: See that color? Cherry going to straw. Slow today. The iron's been cold all morning. Bram says damp. I still say 'NOW!'
event.juno_heart2.1.why: uneasy: cold iron, an ordinary excuse she half believes

event.juno_heart2.4.text: Bram's mark is on every bar in here. Mine's still a sketch. Funny: your great-uncle once asked for a piece with no mark at all.
event.juno_heart2.4.why: hint: echoes the brass key without naming it; why would anyone want it unsigned?

event.juno_heart5.1.text: A steel sword. For the mines, or the weeds. ...Keep it by your door, maybe. No reason. It's yours.
event.juno_heart5.1.why: frightened: the joke about the porch drops; she just wants the player safer

event.juno_heart5.1.text: A steel sword. For the mines, or the weeds, or the walk home. Everyone's walking home early lately. It's yours.
event.juno_heart5.1.why: uneasy: notices the village's early nights, explains nothing

event.juno_heart5.2.text: Don't lose it! ...Your great-uncle wanted a sword once. Then he changed his mind and asked for a tiny key instead.
event.juno_heart5.2.why: clue: what made Edmund trade a weapon for a key?

event.next_door.0.text: Okay, okay, okay. Eyes shut. ...No, keep them open, actually. You look like you've had enough dark. Now!
event.next_door.0.why: uneasy: the surprise ritual bends around the player's nerves

event.next_door.1.text: My own piece, with my own mark. A plain hinge. ...It's still warm, see? Something warm that's yours. I love it more than breakfast!
event.next_door.1.why: frightened: she offers warmth as comfort without knowing why it is needed

event.hall_dance.8.text: Those door hinges are mine. Listen to them swing. ...Stand by me, near the lamps. Everyone's here. Nobody's going anywhere tonight.
event.hall_dance.8.why: frightened: the celebration holds; she keeps the player inside the light

event.hall_dance.8.text: Those door hinges are mine, my mark on every pin. Tilda keeps shutting the woods-side door. I keep opening it. Let it show off!
event.hall_dance.8.why: uneasy: a Keeper's too-exact care, seen by someone who thinks it is fussiness

event.story_notes_juno.intro.text: Don't look! ...Okay, you looked. Fine. Encouragement leaks out of me. Lately everyone looks like they need some. You most.
event.story_notes_juno.intro.why: uneasy: the village is tired and she has noticed

dlg.story.notes.juno.0.text: Juno has a folded note halfway under a door. She stops. So do you. Past the square, a dog barks and barks at the trees.
dlg.story.notes.juno.0.why: frightened: the world ladder (dogs and the wood) at the edge of a warm moment

event.story_notes_juno.after.text: Bram's had six. He keeps every one in his apron pocket. Dr. Penn got one too. She read it at her window, facing the woods.
event.story_notes_juno.after.why: hint: a Keeper's habit noticed as a curiosity

dlg.story.band.talk.1.text: Exhibit B: three anvils, the wash bucket, and Bram, hitting one thing once. The anvils ring flat tonight. I tuned them twice!
dlg.story.band.talk.1.why: uneasy: the music is slightly off, the human version of the hum

dlg.story.band.talk.r1.text: We won! Bram, we won! ...Bram? He stopped. Everyone's looking at the trees. Okay! Clap louder, everyone!
dlg.story.band.talk.r1.why: frightened: the square turns toward the wood; Juno fills the silence on purpose

event.juno_heart4.setup.text: Freeze! Right there. Don't move. Don't move. ...Sorry, that came out wrong. It's a sticky surprise, that's all.
event.juno_heart4.setup.why: frightened: allowed distortion (a repeated phrase) she catches and softens

event.juno_heart4.prank.text: Done! You're labeled! 'Guest (Excellent)'. I nearly wrote 'Guest (Tired)'. You look tired. Spelled right and everything.
event.juno_heart4.prank.why: uneasy: the joke still lands, with a kind glance at the player

dlg.juno.label.r0.text: Accepted! You're a fixture now. Next I'm labeling the whole village. Except the forest gate. Nobody will let me near the forest gate.
dlg.juno.label.r0.why: hint: points at the gate without explaining it

event.juno_heart6.intro.text: Don't come in. Okay, come in. Shut the door, the cold keeps getting in. I made something, it's crooked, and the quench barrel is looking at it.
event.juno_heart6.intro.why: uneasy: cold where the forge should be warmest

dlg.juno.strike.0.text: My first piece that isn't a copy. A little horseshoe. Lopsided. ...It came out of the fire cold. Iron isn't supposed to do that.
dlg.juno.strike.0.why: frightened: the one thing she trusts behaves wrongly; she says so plainly

event.juno_heart6.after.text: It's still crooked. It's still mine. ...I forged it on the fourth night of the season. The fire sulked the whole time. Don't tell Bram yet.
event.juno_heart6.after.why: hint: the same nights every season; a curious player checks the calendar

event.juno_heart8.intro.text: Okay, okay, okay. Today's the right day. I'm showing Bram the horseshoe. Stand next to me? We both look like we didn't sleep.

dlg.juno.shoe.c0.text: Wait with her. Don't look at the window.
dlg.juno.shoe.c0.why: frightened: same choice (wait), the player's own unease leaks into it

dlg.juno.shoe.r0.text: ...Okay. Quiet's good. Everyone is so quiet. So quiet. ...No. Good quiet. This is the good kind. Stay.
dlg.juno.shoe.r0.why: frightened: a short repeated-word stammer, then she chooses the warm reading

event.juno_heart10.intro.text: Hold out your hand. Both hands. The last tiny thing I made for a Fenn was a key. This one has my mark on it.
event.juno_heart10.intro.why: clue: ties the heirloom to Edmund's key; where is that key now?

event.juno_heart10.intro.text: Hold out your hand. Both hands. They're like ice! I made a mark, my own, and I stamped it before I told a single person.
event.juno_heart10.intro.why: uneasy: she notices the player is cold

event.juno_friend.doing.text: See? 'Swimming Pool (Official)'. Quench won't go near it lately. Just sits on the roof facing the woods. Quench has opinions now.
event.juno_friend.doing.why: uneasy: animals face the wood, told as cat gossip

event.juno_friend.wrap.text: Best pool in Wetherell. Only pool. Still a bucket. ...Come by on Thursdays anyway? It's nice, having you where I can see you.
event.juno_friend.wrap.why: frightened: the invitation becomes a check-in

event.juno_birthday.intro.text: Okay, okay, okay, it's my birthday and I'm not nervous! I labeled the cake 'Cake (Birthday)'. Come in, quick, the fog's coming down early!
event.juno_birthday.intro.why: uneasy: the long fog, mentioned in passing

dlg.juno.birthday.0.text: So? What's the plan? There's a plan, right? ...You don't need one. Just stay for cake. Stay a while.
dlg.juno.birthday.0.why: frightened: her shipped excitement line softens into an invitation to rest

event.juno_courtship.intro.text: Okay, okay, okay. I made a list. 'Reasons I Like the Farmer.' Forty items. I wrote it on nights I couldn't sleep. So. Would you court me?
event.juno_courtship.intro.why: uneasy: nobody sleeps well; same question

dlg.juno.courtship.r2.text: Think! Yes! Take your time! I'll be right here, keeping the fire high, not watching the door. Come back before dark, okay?
dlg.juno.courtship.r2.why: frightened: same answer (later); her care shows

event.juno_courtship2.intro.text: The list has forty-one items now. Forty-one is 'patient'. I've been patient through a lot of long nights! So. Would you court me?
event.juno_courtship2.intro.why: uneasy: the long nights, same question

dlg.juno.partners.0.text: Bram banked the forge early and shooed me out. He does that on the dark nights now. The afternoon's ours. What are we doing?
dlg.juno.partners.0.why: uneasy: an unaware man's habit changing too; nobody explains

dlg.juno.partners.r1.text: The beach! With sand! Far from the trees! I'll bring a clasp for luck, and a sandwich. Not for the clasp.
dlg.juno.partners.r1.why: hint: she prefers the shore without saying why

event.overheard_juno_bram_1.l3.text: That's what labels are for! I labeled the back door 'Shut (After Dark)'. Tilda's idea!
event.overheard_juno_bram_1.l3.why: uneasy: a Keeper's rule repeated as a label

event.overheard_juno_bram_2.l3.text: That's the nicest label anyone's made me! ...Make one for the farmer. They look worn.
event.overheard_juno_bram_2.l3.why: frightened: the village talks about the player kindly behind their back

event.overheard_juno_bram_3.l1.text: Bram! Fixed your bench. Crooked joint, don't look. Marcus ordered nails again, day four. Who builds on day four?
event.overheard_juno_bram_3.l1.why: hint: a Keeper's errand on the ritual day, keeps the crooked joint for Bram's reply

event.overheard_juno_bram_4.l3.text: You would? Daily? Even when the nights get long? Even the crooked bench?
event.overheard_juno_bram_4.l3.why: uneasy: a small shadow on a sure promise

event.overheard_piper_juno_1.l2.text: Quieter? Piper, it's a forge! ...Though the anvil keeps ringing after I stop. Is that you?
event.overheard_piper_juno_1.l2.why: uneasy: the hum, heard as a ringing

event.overheard_piper_juno_2.l4.text: That's a hit! 'Song (Forge)'! ...That bit you hum at the end, the four notes. Where's it from?
event.overheard_piper_juno_2.l4.why: hint: points at Edmund's four notes without answering

event.overheard_tilda_juno_1.l3.text: Is the smiley face worth extra? It took an hour. Why'd you close early last new moon?
event.overheard_tilda_juno_1.l3.why: hint: Tilda's answer stays the same, so it reads as a dodge

event.overheard_tilda_juno_3.l3.text: In Wetherell. Definitely. Next door to Bram, with good thick doors. Okay, definitely.
event.overheard_tilda_juno_3.l3.why: uneasy: even her dream forge wants a sturdy door

adds.text: ...You've gone pale. Sit on the bucket a second. Forges do that to people. Stand where it's warm.
adds.why: the unaware villager as ordinary human comfort

adds.text: Eleven evenings, and I left before dark every one. Tilda's lamp tells me when. Don't ask me why I listen to a lamp.
adds.why: a Keeper's tell seen from the outside as a quirk

adds.text: First mark I ever left off was on your great-uncle's key. He asked for it plain. Nothing to say who made it. I still wonder why.
adds.why: clue: echoes the key thread at her proudest moment

adds.text: ...I already wrote you one. It just says 'Sleep'. You look like you haven't.
adds.why: frightened: encouragement turned toward the player's state

cuts.why: the 'thank you or ow' joke falls flat on a frightened player; the added line about looking pale fills the beat

threads.juno_heart6: What happens on the fourth night of every season that makes the forge fire sulk?
threads.juno_heart8: What is the player afraid to see through the forge window?
threads.juno_heart10: Juno made something small for the last Fenn too; where did Edmund's key end up?
threads.juno_friend: Why has the forge cat started watching the woods?
threads.juno_birthday: Why does the fog come down early, even on a birthday?

notes: Small inventions to confirm against LORE.md: Edmund asked for the key unmarked/plain (heart2 hint, next_door add); Edmund first wanted a sword, then the key (heart5 clue); the Community Hall has a 'woods-side door' Tilda keeps shut (hall_dance); Juno's back-door label 'Shut (After Dark)' is Tilda's idea; Marcus ordering nails on day four; Bram banking early on dark nights (Bram is unaware, so it reads as habit, no explanation).
Lines with {if} branches (heart4.reaction, heart8.after, heart10.give/thanks, birthday.after, courtship/courtship2.after, partners.after) are left without variants so the branches survive.
Juno never explains anything; all clue-tier text is things she saw or made, never a theory.
